Subject: Skyline Health — consumption concession ask (SK-438)

Chloe,

Quick context: Skyline (Aisha Khan, procurement) is pushing hard on price — they've asked for a 35% off list rate for Hosted consumption for the first 12 months in exchange for a 36-month committed consumption contract and a roadmap commitment to evaluate Redwood Dedicated in Q3. They are an attractive strategic customer (regional health system, multiple lines of business) and forecasted TCV is ~$4.2M with ARR ramp.

Why they asked: competitor pricing in procurement RFP came in lower; they want parity + extra credits for migration. They are willing to sign a longer-term commitment and add a committed dedicated cluster in year 2 if we can bridge the initial economics.

Attached: proposal_v3.xlsx (pricing + terms), skyline_map.pdf (mutual action plan).

Ask: This is above the 20% concession threshold. Can you escalate for exec signoff? My recommendation: authorize up to 30% now with a finance/ops guardrail (usage floors, staged billing, true-up) — gives us negotiating room and preserves margin.

If helpful I can pull the detailed cost model; Priyom I cc'd for deal-desk input.

Thanks,
Ben

Ben —

Thanks for the summary. I reviewed the attached proposal and MAP. Two quick thoughts:

- We should prioritize locking a minimum committed spend for the first 12 months and include clear usage floors / true-up cadence. That materially reduces downside.
- Given Skyline's willingness to convert to Dedicated later, we should ask for an implementation/PO milestone that triggers the deeper discount tiers.

I'm okay escalating to leadership for a concession that exceeds 20%, but I want to be explicit on the guardrails. Please include the finance cost model and a brief note on how this concession impacts unit economics by quarter. Priyom — can you run the model and propose a structured fallback (e.g., month 7 true-up or automatic re-price if usage < 70% of committed)?

I've attached a short one-pager framing the ask for leadership (proposal_highlight_SK-438.pdf). I'll prepare the email to Mina once we have the cost numbers.

Chloe

Subject: RE: Skyline Health — consumption concession ask (SK-438)

Chloe/Ben —

I ran the numbers and attached cost_model_SK-438.xlsx. TL;DR: a 35% off list for year 1 would reduce gross margin below acceptable thresholds given their expected initial ramp (we would break even only if they hit 140% of committed usage in Q2). A 30% concession with a 36-month commit gives us acceptable NPV (TCV ~$4.2M) and two operational safety nets: 1) a 6-month hard true-up; 2) minimum monthly consumption floors for months 1–12.

Recommended structured concession:
- Year 1: 30% off hosted consumption list rate, subject to monthly floor = 65% of projected consumption (true-up at month 6).
- Year 2–3: step-down discounts tied to committed volume and migration milestone to Dedicated (if not achieved, re-price to standard tier).
- Contractual clauses: audit rights, audit window, and termination fee if usage < 40% of committed in first 6 months.

I also added a short finance note for leadership. HubSpot deal link: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/1234567 (SK-438).

If leadership signs off on 30%, legal needs to draft the amendment with the guardrails above.

- Priyom
